done_when: no live relative markdown link in docs/docs/features/ points at a nonexistent file, and a gate in .proof-os/gates/ naming F-0807 goes RED when a dead link is planted

evidence.command: bash .proof-os/gates/F-0807-doc-links-resolve.sh, plus thirteen probes run one at a time in an isolated copy
evidence.result: zero dead links across thirty-one feature docs; a planted dead link, a directory target and a nested dead link each turn it red, while eight valid shapes and a correction marker quoting a dead link all stay green. The fenced-code and quoted-marker cases were reproduced independently by the dispatcher.

not_checked: a link whose text is split across two source lines by a soft break is not seen; none exists in the tree today, and it is declared in the gate's own NOT CHECKED block rather than left silent
anchor fragments on links that DO resolve, and external http/mailto links, are not verified
doc trees outside docs/docs/features/ - wiki/, top-level READMEs, .proof-os/tasks - are unscanned, and the reviewer notes dead links are likely there too
the docs site was never built, so 'resolves' is judged by CommonMark semantics and the filesystem, not by the real renderer
whether proof-os treats this gate's exit 2 as non-blocking - if it does, deleting docs/docs/features/ entirely would pass silently
the corrected prose itself - this task verified link resolution and excision quality, not whether the surrounding claims are true
